title: Daoism as a Religion
objective: After this level you can explain Daoist temples, priests and rituals, and the Daoist aims of harmony with the Dao and long life.
summary: Daoists date their organized religion to a revelation in 142 CE. Priests with families and celibate monks lead rituals like the jiao, aiming at long life and union with the Dao.

cards.headline: Priests chant in the temple while a parade winds through the streets.
cards.body: It's a Daoist Offering, one of the religion's great rituals. Who are the priests, and what are they working toward?

cards.headline: A revelation in 142 CE
cards.body: Daoists trace their organized religion to a revelation. By tradition, in 142 CE Laozi, worshipped as Lord Lao, appeared to Zhang Daoling and founded the Way of the Celestial Masters. The founding story comes first; the priests and rituals follow.

cards.headline: Priests with families, monks in abbeys
cards.body: The main leader of Daoist ritual is the daoshi, "Daoist master", a role typically passed down within families. Celestial Masters priests marry and live with their families. Quanzhen, found mainly in northern China, is a celibate order of monks and nuns; its White Cloud Abbey in Beijing is the seat of the China Daoist Association. Two ways to serve, one tradition.

cards.headline: The Offering
cards.body: The Offering, jiao, renews the bond between a community and its gods. It usually lasts one to ten days. Inside the temple, priests perform the ritual; outside, a street festival carries the local god's statue through the neighborhood. Another ritual, Merit (gongde), is a funeral rite. Temple and street work as one.

cards.headline: Long life and the Dao
cards.body: What is it all for? "Long life" and "immortality" are among the most recurrent words in Daoist writing, and liberation is often pictured as union with the Dao. Immortals are said to be people who went beyond the limits of ordinary human life, usually through their practices. Quanzhen monks practice meditation and Internal Alchemy (neidan).

cards.headline: Daoism as a Religion: the takeaways
learned: Daoists date their organized religion to a revelation in 142 CE
Celestial Masters priests marry; Quanzhen monks and nuns are celibate
The jiao renews a community's bond with its gods

questions.prompt: According to Daoist tradition, _____ appeared to Zhang Daoling in 142 CE.

options.label: Confucius, as a teacher
options.rationale: Confucius isn't part of this founding story.

options.label: the Buddha, from India
options.rationale: The revelation came from Lord Lao.

options.label: an emperor of the Han dynasty
options.rationale: Tradition names a divine figure, not an emperor.

questions.explanation: By tradition, Lord Lao appeared to Zhang Daoling and founded the Way of the Celestial Masters.

questions.prompt: How, in Daoist tradition, did the immortals reach their state?

options.label: By going beyond ordinary human limits, usually through their practices
By being born into royal families
options.rationale: Practice, not birth, is the path described.

options.label: By memorizing every one of the Confucian and Daoist classics word for word
options.rationale: That isn't the Daoist path described here.

questions.explanation: Immortals are said to be people who went beyond ordinary limits, usually by means of their practices.

questions.prompt: A jiao has priests in the temple and a festival in the street. Which two of Level 3's seven dimensions does the jiao show most clearly?

options.label: Doctrine and experience
options.rationale: The jiao is something people do together.

options.label: Ethics and narrative
options.rationale: The jiao is a rite, not a law or story.

options.label: The material side and doctrine
options.rationale: The statue matters, but the rite and the community are the core.

questions.explanation: The priests' rite is Smart's ritual dimension; the whole neighborhood taking part is the social side.
